newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $63- feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $63- feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle traded in light volume at $63.00 per cwt on Friday, unchanged from moderate sales this week, but down $1.00 from last week, feedlot sources said.
An estimated 1,200 head sold in the Texas/Oklahoma Panhandle area, including 700 steers and 500 heifers, following weekly movement of 85,700 head, USDA said.

Kansas trade was quiet, with not enough slaughter cattle sold for a market test. Weekly volume totalled 62,700 head, including 17,500 or about 28 percent previously contracted or formulated cattle, USDA reported.
Scattered packer bids at $63.00 were passed by owners still holding cattle from this week's showlists. They were pricing market-ready animals at $64.00 to $65.00, sources said.
The owners were holding cattle over until next week because weights continue to run light and on ideas that packers were short bought and will need cattle early next week.
Feedlot cattle prices next week, however, could slip another $1.00 if beef demand sputters, some sources said.
